q: Inventory Management 基础需求包含哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which capabilities belong in the base inventory management design?
options: 跨多个仓库跟踪产品库存
按仓库 add/remove stock
查询哪些仓库可满足某产品数量
仓库间 transfer stock
低库存告警和线程安全
options_en: Track product stock across multiple warehouses.
Add or remove stock at a specific warehouse.
Query which warehouses can fulfill a given quantity.
Transfer stock between warehouses.
Fire low-stock alerts and stay thread-safe.
why: 题目核心是库存数量、跨仓库协调、低库存通知和并发正确性；产品目录、订单支付、持久化都被排除。
why_en: The base inventory system tracks stock across warehouses, supports add/remove/transfer/availability, fires low-stock alerts, and must be thread-safe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个线程同时调用同一段代码时结果依然正确，不会出现数据损坏或丢更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thread-safe means the result stays correct even when multiple threads call the code at the same time.

optionExplanations: 多仓库场景下必须按仓库分别记录数量，不然无法判断哪个仓库能发货。
add/remove 是库存变化的基本操作，缺了它仓库数量永远无法更新。
下单前要知道哪些仓库能凑够这个数量，这个查询是履约路径的前提。
仓库间调货要保证不多不少地转移，属于核心而非可选功能。
库存要在高并发下保持正确，同时低库存要能主动通知，这两者都是不可少的非功能需求。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-warehouse tracking is needed because fulfillment decisions depend on which specific warehouse holds the stock.
Add/remove are the basic mutations; without them a warehouse's quantity can never change.
Checking which warehouses can cover a quantity is what the fulfillment path needs before placing an order.
Transferring stock between warehouses must move the exact amount, not just add to one side.
Staying correct under concurrency and proactively alerting on low stock are both non-negotiable requirements here.

scenario: 产品目录由外部系统管理，本系统只收到 productId 并记录数量。
scenario_en: The product catalog is owned by another system; this service only receives a productId and tracks quantity.
q: Product 应如何建模？
q_en: How should Product be modeled in this inventory system?
options: 作为 string 或整数 key，而不是实体类
完整 Product 类，包含名称、图片和价格
AlertListener 的子类
Warehouse 的内部锁
options_en: As a string or integer key, not an entity class.
A full Product class with name, image, and price.
A subclass of AlertListener.
An internal lock owned by Warehouse.
why: 本系统不管理产品生命周期或属性，只按 productId 计数；把外部目录建成实体会扩大范围。
why_en: Product stays a plain key because catalog management and product attributes live outside the inventory system.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求加入产品创建、分类、属性校验或生命周期管理，Product 才值得成为实体类。
tradeoff: Product 作为外部 key vs Product 作为本地实体类

termDefinitions.meaning: 拥有独立状态和行为、值得被建成一个类的对象，而不是别的类里的一个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entity class is an object with its own state and behavior that deserves to be modeled as a class, not just a field.

optionExplanations: 本系统不管产品名称或价格这些属性，只需要 productId 当查找库存的钥匙就够。
只有当这个系统真要管产品创建、分类和属性校验时，才值得把 Product 升级成带名称、图片、价格的实体类。
AlertListener 是通知回调接口，跟“这是哪个产品”完全是两回事，把 Product 挂在它下面没有意义。
锁是用来保护并发访问的机制，不是拿来表示产品身份，把 Product 当成锁混淆了两个概念。
optionExplanations_en: This service never touches a product's name or price, so a plain productId key is enough to look up stock.
A full Product entity only earns its keep once the system owns creation, categorization, or attribute validation.
AlertListener is the notification callback interface — it has nothing to do with what a product is.
A lock protects concurrent access; it has no business representing what a product is.

q: 最终设计中的核心类型有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core types belong in the final inventory design?
options: InventoryManager
Warehouse
AlertConfig
AlertListener
options_en: InventoryManager, the multi-warehouse orchestrator.
Warehouse, a single storage location.
AlertConfig, pairing a threshold with a listener.
AlertListener, the notification callback interface.
why: Manager 负责编排多仓库操作，Warehouse 管单仓库存量和告警，AlertConfig/AlertListener 解耦阈值和通知动作。
why_en: The design uses an InventoryManager, per-location Warehouses, AlertConfig value objects, and an AlertListener interface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统唯一入口，持有全部 Warehouse 并负责跨仓库协调（transfer、availability）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InventoryManager is the single entry point that owns every Warehouse and coordinates cross-warehouse work like transfer and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表一个物理仓储地点，持有自己的库存 map 和告警配置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Warehouse represents one physical storage location and owns its own inventory map and alert configs.

optionExplanations: InventoryManager 是唯一入口，靠它才能按 warehouseId 路由到具体仓库并协调跨仓操作。
Warehouse 是库存状态真正的拥有者，每个仓库自己的数量变化都在这里发生。
AlertConfig 把阈值和 listener 绑定成一对，让一个产品能配置多条告警规则。
作为通知回调的抽象接口，它让 Warehouse 不用关心具体是邮件还是 webhook。
optionExplanations_en: InventoryManager is the single entry point that routes to the right warehouse and coordinates cross-warehouse work.
Warehouse is the real owner of stock state — every quantity change for that location happens here.
AlertConfig pairs a threshold with a listener so one product can carry several alert rules at once.
It's the callback abstraction that keeps Warehouse from caring whether notification means email or a webhook.

q: InventoryManager 为什么保存 Map<string, Warehouse>？
q_en: Why does InventoryManager keep a Map<string, Warehouse>?
options: 为了替代每个 Warehouse 自己的 inventory map
按 warehouseId 做 O(1) 路由到 Warehouse
为了触发所有告警监听器
为了按产品名给仓库排序
options_en: To replace each Warehouse's own inventory map.
To route by warehouseId in O(1) time to the right Warehouse.
To fire every alert listener at once.
To sort warehouses by product name.
why: 外部调用用 warehouseId 指定目标仓库，map 给出 O(1) 查找；list 扫描也能做，但意图和效率都不如 map。
why_en: InventoryManager keeps a warehouse map so it can route by warehouseId in constant time instead of scanning a list.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复杂度记号，表示操作耗时不随数据量增长，例如 map 按 key 查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means constant time: the operation's cost does not grow as the data set gets bigger, like a map lookup by key.

optionExplanations: InventoryManager 的 map 存的是仓库对象本身，跟每个 Warehouse 内部自己的库存数据是两层完全不同的东西。
调用方传进来的是 warehouseId，用它当 key 直接查表就能拿到对应仓库，不用一个个仓库比对。
触发告警监听器是 Warehouse 内部 alertConfigs 的职责，跟 Manager 怎么存仓库列表无关。
这个 map 的 key 是 warehouseId 不是产品名，它从设计上就没有承担排序的用途。
optionExplanations_en: InventoryManager's map holds warehouse objects, a different layer entirely from each Warehouse's own inventory data.
Callers hand in a warehouseId, and using it as a key gets a direct lookup instead of comparing against every warehouse.
Firing alert listeners is alertConfigs' job inside Warehouse, unrelated to how Manager stores its warehouse list.
The map keys on warehouseId, not product name, so sorting by name was never part of what it's for.

scenario: 一个 Warehouse 要保存每个 productId 的当前库存，并支持产品不存在时视为 0。
scenario_en: One Warehouse must track the current quantity for each productId, with missing products treated as zero.
q: Warehouse 记录库存该用什么数据结构？
q_en: What data structure should Warehouse use for stock counts?
options: 单个 totalQuantity 整数
List<InventoryManager>
Map<productId,int> inventory
Map<Warehouse,AlertListener>
options_en: A single totalQuantity integer.
A List<InventoryManager>.
A Map<productId,int> called inventory.
A Map<Warehouse,AlertListener>.
why: 每个产品数量独立变化，需要按 productId 查找和更新；未出现过的产品默认按 0 处理。
why_en: Warehouse needs a productId-to-quantity map because each product's stock changes independently and missing products default to zero.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个仓库真的只卖一种产品，单个整数就够；多产品库存必须用 map。
tradeoff: 按产品建 map vs 单一总量整数
optionExplanations: 一个整数只能表示总量，分不清哪个产品各有多少，一旦仓库卖多种产品就不够用。
InventoryManager 是编排者，不是仓库存的库存条目，把它塞进这里类型上就不对。
每个产品的数量各自独立变化，要能按产品单独查、单独改，天然对应 Map<productId,int> 这个结构。
这个类型是把仓库映射到监听器，跟“这个仓库有多少某产品”完全是不同的信息。
optionExplanations_en: A single integer only tracks a grand total, losing per-product counts once a warehouse stocks more than one item.
InventoryManager is the orchestrator, not a stock entry a warehouse holds — the type itself is a mismatch.
Every product's own count can rise or fall on its own schedule and needs its own lookup and update, which a Map<productId,int> shape captures directly.
That type maps warehouses to listeners, which is a completely different piece of information than per-product stock.

q: Warehouse 需要直接持有哪些字段？（多选）
q_en: Which fields should Warehouse directly own?
options: id
inventory: Map<string,int>
alertConfigs: Map<string,List<AlertConfig>>
其他仓库列表
options_en: id, the warehouse's own identifier.
inventory: Map<string,int> for per-product quantity.
alertConfigs: Map<string,List<AlertConfig>> for alert rules.
A list of every other warehouse.
why: Warehouse 管理一个地点自己的库存和告警配置；跨仓库视角属于 InventoryManager，不属于 Warehouse。
why_en: Warehouse owns its ID, product quantities, and product-specific alert configs, not the whole fleet of warehouses.
optionExplanations: id 让这个仓库能在告警和路由里被唯一识别出来。
inventory 是这个仓库自己产品数量的真实来源，必须直接持有。
alertConfigs 记录这个仓库每个产品的告警规则，也是仓库自己的状态。
跨仓库这类协调工作应该交给 Manager 处理，Warehouse 自己囤一份其他仓库的列表就管到了不该管的地方。
optionExplanations_en: id lets this warehouse be uniquely identified in routing and alerts.
inventory is the source of truth for this warehouse's own product counts, so it must live here directly.
alertConfigs holds this warehouse's own per-product alert rules, also local state.
Knowing about every other warehouse is InventoryManager's coordination job — Warehouse holding that list oversteps its role.

scenario: 同一产品可能有 50 件预警和 10 件紧急告警，并通知不同渠道。
scenario_en: The same product may have a warning at 50 units and an urgent alert at 10 units, each notifying a different channel.
q: alertConfigs 为什么设计成 productId -> List<AlertConfig>？
q_en: Why is alertConfigs modeled as productId to List<AlertConfig>?
options: 因为每个产品只能有一个告警
为了替代库存数量本身
为了把仓库 ID 存成 list
支持同一产品配置多个阈值和 listener
options_en: Because each product can only have one alert.
To replace the stock quantity itself.
To store warehouse IDs as a list.
To support multiple thresholds and listeners per product.
why: 多个阈值可对应不同通知渠道；AlertConfig 把 threshold 和 listener 成对保存，避免用并行数组表达。
why_en: alertConfigs maps to a list because one product can have several thresholds, each paired with its own listener.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个产品从不需要区分预警和紧急两级，单一阈值字段就够，不必用 list。
tradeoff: list 支持多阈值 vs 单一阈值字段更简单

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 threshold 和 listener 绑定在一起的轻量值对象，一个产品可以有多个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AlertConfig is a small value object pairing a threshold with the listener to notify, and one product can have several.

optionExplanations: 场景里一个产品同时有预警和紧急两级告警，说明一个产品显然可以有不止一条规则。
库存数量存在 inventory map 里，alertConfigs 管的是告警规则，两者职责不重叠。
这个 map 的 value 是 AlertConfig 列表，不是仓库 ID，跟仓库标识毫无关系。
同一产品要支持不同阈值对应不同通知渠道，list 让多条规则可以并存而不用并行数组。
optionExplanations_en: The scenario itself pairs one product with both a warning and an urgent alert, which already proves a product can carry more than a single rule.
Stock quantity lives in the inventory map; alertConfigs governs alert rules, a separate concern entirely.
This map's value is a list of AlertConfig, not warehouse IDs — it has nothing to do with warehouse identity.
Letting a single product carry more than one alert rule, each wired to its own channel, needs a list instead of parallel arrays.

scenario: Warehouse 触发低库存通知时，只调用一个抽象接口的方法，不关心具体实现是邮件还是 webhook。
scenario_en: When Warehouse fires a low-stock notification, it calls an abstract interface and does not know whether the implementation sends email or a webhook.
q: AlertListener 接口体现了什么设计原则？
q_en: Which design principle does the AlertListener interface show?
options: Observer + DIP：只依赖通知抽象，不依赖具体实现
Singleton：整个进程运行期间全局只有一个监听器实例
Composite：把多个监听器组合成一整棵仓库树形结构
Factory：由一个专门的工厂类负责创建库存对象
options_en: Observer plus DIP: depend only on the notification abstraction, not a concrete implementation.
Singleton: exactly one listener instance exists for the whole running process.
Composite: listeners are composed into one tree structure spanning every warehouse.
Factory: a dedicated factory class is responsible for constructing inventory objects.
why: Warehouse 只调用 onLowStock，具体邮件、webhook、日志由实现决定，这是 Observer 模式，也满足依赖倒置。
why_en: AlertListener is the Observer pattern applying dependency inversion: Warehouse depends only on the callback interface, not a concrete notifier.
tradeoff: 依赖抽象接口 vs 依赖具体通知实现

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象状态变化时通知一组监听者，被通知方自己决定如何响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern notifies a set of listeners when state changes, and each listener decides how to react.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高层模块依赖抽象接口而不是具体实现，方便替换底层实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP, the Dependency Inversion Principle, means high-level modules depend on an abstraction instead of a concrete implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证一个类在系统里全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern guarantees a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象组合成树形结构，单个对象和组合对象用同一接口处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Composite pattern combines objects into tree structures so individual and composite objects share the same interface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象创建逻辑封装起来，调用方不需要知道具体构造细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern encapsulates object creation so callers do not need to know construction details.

optionExplanations: Warehouse 只认识 onLowStock 这一个抽象方法，具体谁来实现、怎么发通知它完全不关心，这正是 Observer 配合依赖倒置。
Singleton 保证的是全局只有一个实例，跟这里可以插拔任意通知实现完全是两个诉求。
Composite 是把对象拼成树形结构、按同一接口统一处理，这里没有仓库组合成树的场景。
Factory 管的是对象怎么被创建出来，AlertListener 的重点是通知怎么被调用，跟创建逻辑无关。
optionExplanations_en: Warehouse only knows the abstract onLowStock method and never cares who implements it or how — that is Observer plus dependency inversion.
Singleton guarantees one global instance, a different goal from letting any notifier implementation be plugged in here.
Composite combines objects into a tree handled through one shared interface, and there is no warehouse tree here.
Factory is about how an object gets constructed, while this pattern is about how a notification gets invoked — different concerns.

q: 补全 AlertConfig 的职责：
q_en: Complete the responsibility of AlertConfig:
text: AlertConfig 是把 {{threshold}} 和 {{AlertListener}} 绑定在一起的轻量值对象。
why: 它让配置关系显式化。看到 List<AlertConfig> 就知道这是多个低库存告警规则。
why_en: AlertConfig pairs a low-stock threshold with the listener that should be notified.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只承载数据、没有独立身份或生命周期管理的轻量对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A value object is a lightweight object that just carries data without its own identity or lifecycle.

scenario: 调用 getWarehousesWithAvailability('WIDGET', 100)，需要知道哪些仓库各自能凑够 100 件。
scenario_en: A call to getWarehousesWithAvailability('WIDGET', 100) asks which individual warehouses can each supply 100 units.
q: InventoryManager 应如何实现该方法？
q_en: How should InventoryManager implement this availability lookup?
options: 只检查列表里第一个仓库的库存就直接返回结果
遍历每个 Warehouse，收集能满足数量的 ID
把所有仓库的库存直接相加后只返回一个 ID
先把库存扣减掉，再统计剩下的数量并返回
options_en: Check only the first warehouse in the list and return right away.
Iterate every Warehouse and collect the IDs that can fulfill the quantity.
Sum stock across every warehouse and hand back just one ID.
Deduct the stock first, then count and return whatever is left.
why: 需求问的是“哪些仓库各自能满足数量”，不是系统总量；Manager 负责跨仓库聚合结果。
why_en: Availability checks each warehouse independently and returns the IDs that can fulfill the quantity on their own.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求变成跨仓拆单 fulfill，则要返回一个组合方案而不只是单仓库列表。
tradeoff: 逐仓库独立判断 vs 系统总量聚合
optionExplanations: 只看第一个仓库会漏掉后面明明能满足数量的仓库，跟需求“哪些仓库各自能凑够”不符。
需求问的是每个仓库各自能不能凑够数量，只有逐个检查再收集满足条件的 ID 才能给出这个答案。
把库存加总只能回答系统总量够不够，答不出具体是哪个仓库这个问题。
这只是一个只读查询，真的去扣库存会产生副作用，完全偏离了查询本身的语义。
optionExplanations_en: Stopping at the first warehouse misses others that could genuinely cover the requested amount, missing what the query actually asks.
The question is which warehouses can each cover the amount by themselves, so checking every one and collecting the qualifying IDs is the only way to answer it.
Summing stock only tells you whether the system total is enough, not which specific warehouse can do it.
This is meant to be a read-only lookup; actually deducting stock introduces a side effect the query was never supposed to have.

scenario: Warehouse 当前只有 2 个 WIDGET，请求 removeStock('WIDGET', 10)。
scenario_en: The Warehouse currently has only 2 WIDGET units, and removeStock('WIDGET', 10) is called.
q: removeStock 的正确行为是什么？
q_en: What should removeStock do in this case?
options: 把库存设为 -8
先扣再异步补偿差额
返回 false 且库存不变
改为触发 addStock
options_en: Set the quantity to -8.
Deduct first, then compensate the gap asynchronously.
Return false and leave the quantity unchanged.
Silently call addStock instead.
why: 不允许负库存是不变量；removeStock 必须在写入前检查 currentQty >= quantity，不够就直接拒绝。
why_en: removeStock must reject insufficient stock and leave the quantity unchanged instead of ever going negative.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统支持 backorder，可以单独建 reserved/backordered 状态，但不能偷偷让 physical inventory 变负。
tradeoff: 拒绝并保持不变 vs 允许透支后补偿
optionExplanations: 负库存直接打破库存不能为负这条不变量，是最不能接受的处理方式。
先扣再补偿意味着中间会有一段时间库存是错的，给下游一个假象的可用数量。
扣减前先确认 currentQty 是否覆盖这次的 quantity，覆盖不了就直接返回失败、库存原封不动，这是最干净的处理方式。
库存不够时悄悄改成加库存，会让调用方以为扣减成功了，语义完全变了。
optionExplanations_en: Setting it to -8 straight-up breaks the never-go-negative invariant, the least acceptable outcome.
Deducting first and compensating later leaves a window where the count is simply wrong for anyone reading it.
Comparing currentQty against the requested amount before touching anything, and returning failure untouched when it falls short, keeps the state clean.
Silently calling addStock instead makes the caller think the removal succeeded, which changes the method's meaning entirely.

scenario: 实现 Warehouse.removeStock，要求线程安全且不能出现负库存。
scenario_en: Warehouse.removeStock must be thread-safe and must never create negative stock.
q: 这段实现的关键并发保证是什么？
q_en: What concurrency guarantee does this implementation provide?
options: 允许库存直接变成负数，以换取更高吞吐
先触发低库存告警，再去执行库存扣减
这个仓库里每个产品都共用同一把全局锁
检查和扣减在同一把锁内完成，告警在锁外触发
options_en: Allow the quantity to go negative outright in exchange for more throughput.
Fire the low-stock alert first, then go execute the deduction.
Every product in this warehouse shares the exact same global lock.
Check and deduct inside one lock; fire alerts after releasing it.
why: 同一把锁保护 read-modify-write，防止并发扣减穿插；回调放锁外，避免慢 I/O 阻塞库存操作。
why_en: The method keeps validation and mutation atomic under one lock while firing alert callbacks only after releasing it.
whenOtherWins: 如果高吞吐下同仓库不同产品并发很多，可考虑 per-product locks，但复杂度更高。
tradeoff: 仓库级单锁简单 vs per-product 锁并发更高但更复杂
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["lock warehouse"] --> B{"qty valid and enough stock?"}
B -- no --> C["return false"]
B -- yes --> D["update inventory"]
D --> E["collect alerts"]
E --> F["unlock warehouse"]
F --> G["fire listeners outside lock"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读取当前值、再计算新值、最后写回的操作序列；不加保护会被并发穿插。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-modify-write is reading a value, computing a new one, and writing it back, which needs protection under concurrency.

optionExplanations: 允许负库存直接违反不变量，用它换吞吐是拿正确性做交易，不可取。
先通知再扣库存意味着通知发出时库存其实还没变，读者看到的状态跟通知内容对不上。
每个产品都用全局锁等于所有产品共用一把锁，退化成了最粗粒度的串行化，不是这段代码的做法。
校验和扣减放在同一把锁里保证不会被并发穿插，收集完待触发的告警再在锁外调用，慢 I/O 不会拖住库存操作。
optionExplanations_en: Allowing negative stock breaks the invariant outright — trading correctness for throughput is not an option here.
Firing the notification before deducting means the alert goes out while the count hasn't actually changed yet.
A single global lock shared by every product collapses concurrency to the coarsest possible serialization, not what this code does.

Checking the balance and writing the new value share a single lock so no concurrent update can interleave, while the collected alerts fire only after that lock releases so slow I/O never blocks inventory work.

scenario: 阈值是 10，库存持续在 9、8、7 之间波动。
scenario_en: The threshold is 10, and stock keeps moving among 9, 8, and 7.
q: 低库存告警为什么不应“每次 newQty < threshold 都触发”？
q_en: Why should a low-stock alert not fire on every newQty < threshold update?
options: 库存已低于阈值时每次扣减都会重复报警，造成噪音
因为低库存根本不需要通知
因为这样 addStock 就不能改变数量
因为 listener 只能被调用一次
options_en: Once stock is already below threshold, every further deduction re-fires, creating noise.
Because low stock never needs a notification at all.
Because this would stop addStock from changing quantity.
Because a listener can only ever be called once.
why: 持续低库存不是每次变化都值得重复通知；只在从阈值以上跌到阈值以下时报警更可操作。
why_en: Alerting on every below-threshold update spams notifications while the stock remains continuously low.
tradeoff: 每次低于阈值都报警 vs 只在下穿阈值那一刻报警
optionExplanations: 库存持续卡在阈值以下时，每次扣减都会触发一次同样的通知，堆积成没人想看的噪音。
低库存显然需要通知，这正是这套告警机制存在的原因，说不需要通知是反过来的结论。
触发条件是判断阈值有没有被穿越，跟 addStock 还能不能改变数量完全是两件事。
listener 是普通回调，可以被多次调用，限制成只调用一次这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: While stock stays stuck below threshold for a while, every further deduction would re-fire the same alert, piling up into noise nobody wants.
Low stock clearly does need a notification — that's the entire reason this alerting mechanism exists in the first place.
The firing condition is about detecting a threshold crossing, unrelated to whether addStock can still change the quantity.
A listener is an ordinary callback that can be invoked many times; claiming it fires only once just isn't true.

q: 补全阈值穿越条件：
q_en: Complete the threshold-crossing condition:
text: 只有当 previousQty {{>= threshold}} 且 newQty {{< threshold}} 时，才触发低库存告警。
why: 这个条件天然防重复，也天然重置：库存补回阈值以上后，下次跌破会再次触发。
why_en: The downward-crossing condition prevents duplicate alerts and naturally resets after stock recovers.

q: 按顺序排列阈值告警的 reset 行为：
q_en: Put the threshold alert reset behavior in order:
steps: 库存从 15 降到 9，阈值 10，触发告警。
库存从 9 降到 7，不再触发。
库存从 7 补到 22，不触发。
库存从 22 降到 9，再次触发。
why: 没有额外 hasFired 状态，previous/new 的比较就表达了恢复后可再次报警。
why_en: Comparing previous and new quantities gives duplicate prevention and reset behavior without extra state.

scenario: AlertListener 可能发送邮件或调用 webhook，这些都是慢 I/O。
scenario_en: AlertListener may send email or call a webhook, both of which are slow I/O.
q: 为什么不能在 synchronized(this) 内直接调用 listener.onLowStock？
q_en: Why should listener.onLowStock not run inside synchronized(this)?
options: listener 接口本身设计成无法接收任何参数
慢 I/O 会长时间占用仓库锁，甚至回调仓库导致死锁
告警回调必须先于库存写入完成才能执行
Java 这门语言完全不允许接口方法被回调
options_en: The listener interface itself was designed to accept no parameters at all.
Slow I/O holds the warehouse lock too long, and a callback into the warehouse can even deadlock.
The alert callback has to finish before the inventory write is even allowed to run.
The Java language flatly disallows an interface method from ever being called back.
why: 锁内只应做快速内存操作；先收集 alertsToFire，释放锁后再执行外部回调。
why_en: Alert callbacks should run outside the warehouse lock to avoid blocking or deadlocking inventory operations.
whenOtherWins: 如果 listener 保证纯内存、可靠且不会回调仓库，锁内调用也能工作，但生产上不稳。
tradeoff: 锁外触发保吞吐 vs 锁内触发更简单但可能阻塞

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个或多个线程互相等待对方持有的锁，谁都无法继续执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when two or more threads wait forever for locks that each other already holds.

optionExplanations: listener 接口本身能正常接收参数，这跟锁里锁外调用没有关系。
邮件或 webhook 这类慢 I/O 会让仓库锁被长时间占住，如果回调又反过来调用仓库方法，还可能自我死锁。
场景里告警是库存变化之后的结果，顺序反过来在逻辑上说不通。
Java 完全支持在同步块里调用接口方法，这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: A listener interface accepts parameters just fine; that has nothing to do with calling it inside or outside a lock.
Slow I/O like email or a webhook would tie up that lock for a long stretch, and a callback that reaches back into Warehouse itself can even deadlock.
In this scenario the alert is a consequence of the stock change, so running it first would be backwards.
Java has no restriction against calling an interface method inside a synchronized block; that claim is simply false.

q: Warehouse 中哪些 public 方法应同步访问共享状态？（多选）
q_en: Which public Warehouse methods should synchronize access to shared state?
options: addStock
removeStock
getStock
checkAvailability
setLowStockAlert
options_en: addStock
removeStock
getStock
checkAvailability
setLowStockAlert
why: 写方法需要互斥，读方法也要看到一致且最新的库存/配置；统一用仓库锁最容易证明正确。
why_en: All public methods touching warehouse state should synchronize to provide atomicity and consistent, visible reads.
optionExplanations: addStock 修改共享的库存 map，必须在锁保护下写入。
removeStock 既要读也要写库存，读写夹在一起更需要互斥。
getStock 是读操作，但读到的必须是最新一致的值，不同步可能读到中间状态。
checkAvailability 同样要读一致的库存，跟 getStock 面对相同的可见性问题。
setLowStockAlert 修改 alertConfigs 这个共享 map，跟修改库存 map 需要一样的保护。
optionExplanations_en: addStock mutates the shared inventory map, so the write needs the same lock protection.
removeStock both reads and writes stock in one step, which needs mutual exclusion even more than a pure write.
getStock is a read, but it still must see the latest consistent value — an unsynchronized read can catch a half-written state.
checkAvailability faces the same visibility problem as getStock: it needs a consistent read too.
setLowStockAlert mutates the shared alertConfigs map, which needs the same protection as mutating inventory.

scenario: 基础实现给每个 Warehouse 用同一把 synchronized(this) 锁保护所有产品。
scenario_en: The base implementation protects all products in one Warehouse with the same synchronized(this) lock.
q: Warehouse 级粗粒度锁的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of a coarse Warehouse-level lock?
options: 吞吐最高但难以证明正确
会让 removeStock 不再检查库存
简单正确，但同一仓库不同产品的操作不能并行
只适用于单线程程序
options_en: Highest throughput but hard to prove correct.
It stops removeStock from checking stock at all.
Simple and correct, but different products in the same warehouse cannot run in parallel.
Only works in a single-threaded program.
why: 每次操作只是少量 map 访问和告警收集，锁持有时间短；基础范围下清晰性比 per-product 锁的复杂度更重要。
why_en: A warehouse-level lock is simple and correct, though it serializes operations on different products in the same warehouse.
tradeoff: 正确性和简单性 vs 同仓库跨产品并发度
optionExplanations: 粗粒度锁恰恰是吞吐较低但容易证明正确，这个说法把两个属性说反了。
锁的粒度跟 removeStock 要不要检查库存是两件独立的事，加锁不会取消检查逻辑。
锁的正确性容易证明，代价是同一仓库不同产品的操作也会被这把锁串行化，不能并行。
这把锁本身就是为多线程并发设计的，用来保护共享状态，跟单线程程序没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: A coarse lock is actually the low-throughput, easy-to-prove-correct end of the spectrum — this statement flips those two properties.
Lock granularity and whether removeStock still validates stock are independent concerns; locking doesn't remove the check.
The lock is easy to prove correct, but the cost is that two products sharing one warehouse can no longer run in parallel.
This lock exists specifically to protect shared state under concurrency — it has nothing to do with single-threaded programs.

scenario: 同一仓库里不同产品的并发操作极多，warehouse 级锁成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: Different products in the same Warehouse see heavy concurrent operations, and the warehouse-level lock becomes the bottleneck.
q: 更细粒度的优化方案是什么？
q_en: What is the finer-grained locking optimization?
options: 彻底去掉所有锁，完全靠调用方自己保证操作顺序
只给 AlertListener 这一个对象本身单独加锁
把每一个产品都拆分成一个独立的 Warehouse
为每个 productId 配一把独立锁，配合线程安全 map
options_en: Remove every lock entirely and trust callers alone to order operations correctly.
Only put a lock on the AlertListener object itself, nothing else.
Split every single product out into its own separate Warehouse.
Keep one lock per productId alongside a thread-safe map for the shared state.
why: per-product lock 允许不同产品并行操作，但需要线程安全 map、锁生命周期管理和多产品操作的锁顺序。
why_en: Per-product locking improves cross-product concurrency but adds the work of creating, tracking, and releasing each lock in the right order.
whenOtherWins: 如果竞争低或实现时间有限，warehouse 级锁仍是更好的默认选择。
tradeoff: 并发度更高 vs 锁管理和排序复杂度更高

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多线程并发读写而不破坏内部结构的哈希表实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConcurrentHashMap is a hash table implementation that supports concurrent reads and writes without corrupting its internal structure.

optionExplanations: 完全去掉锁只会把竞态条件的责任甩给调用方，并不能真正解决瓶颈问题。
AlertListener 只是通知回调，真正的竞争点在库存 map 的读写，锁错了对象。
把产品拆成独立仓库会让库存概念本身失真，产品和仓库是两个维度，不能互相替代。
给每个 productId 配独立锁，配合线程安全的 map，能让不同产品的操作真正并行，只是要多管理锁的生命周期和顺序。
optionExplanations_en: Removing locking entirely just hands the race condition to callers instead of actually solving the bottleneck.
AlertListener is only the notification callback; the real contention is on reading and writing the inventory map, so this locks the wrong thing.
Splitting every product into its own warehouse distorts what a warehouse even means — product and warehouse are different dimensions.
A lock per productId plus a thread-safe map lets different products run truly in parallel, at the cost of extra bookkeeping for when each lock gets created, held, and released in order.

q: 按顺序排列 naive transfer 的 TOCTOU bug：
q_en: Put the naive transfer TOCTOU bug in order:
steps: 线程 A checkAvailability 看到源仓库有 50 件。
线程 B 在 A remove 前先扣走这 50 件。
线程 A 继续 remove 或忽略失败结果。
线程 A 仍向目标仓库 add 50 件，产生幻影库存或中间状态错误。
why: check 和 use 分属不同临界区，另一个线程可以插入；跨仓库操作需要更强的原子性。
why_en: The naive transfer has a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race between checking and removing stock.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
participant A as Thread A
participant B as Thread B
participant S as Source Warehouse
participant T as Target Warehouse
A->>S: checkAvailability = true
B->>S: remove 50
A->>S: remove or ignore failure
A->>T: add 50
Note over A,T: check and use were not atomic

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件、再据此操作，两步之间状态被别的线程改变，导致检查结果失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TOCTOU, Time-Of-Check-To-Time-Of-Use, is a race where the state changes between checking a condition and acting on it.

scenario: transfer(productId, EAST, WEST, 5) 要求对外表现为原子操作。
scenario_en: transfer(productId, EAST, WEST, 5) must appear atomic to outside callers.
q: 最正确的基础方案是什么？
q_en: What is the best base implementation for atomic transfer?
options: 按稳定顺序同时锁两个 Warehouse，再 remove/add
先执行 remove，晚点再执行 add，全程不锁目标仓库
只检查一遍 availability，但完全不真正扣减库存
先把库存加到目标仓库，再回头检查源仓库够不够
options_en: Lock both warehouses in a stable order, then remove from source and add to destination.
Remove first, add much later, and never lock the destination at all.
Only run an availability check without ever actually deducting stock.
Add to the destination warehouse first, then go back and check the source.
why: 同时持有两把仓库锁能避免外部观察到库存从两个仓库都消失；稳定顺序防止双向 transfer 死锁。
why_en: Atomic transfer locks both warehouses in a consistent order before removing and adding stock.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务接受在途中间状态，应把 Transfer 建成一等实体，而不是假装瞬移。
tradeoff: 双锁强原子性 vs 单锁弱原子性换取更高并发
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["sort warehouse ids"] --> B["lock first warehouse"]
B --> C["lock second warehouse"]
C --> D{"source has enough stock?"}
D -- no --> E["unlock and return false"]
D -- yes --> F["remove from source"]
F --> G["add to target"]
G --> H["unlock and return true"]
optionExplanations: 两把锁一起拿住，观察者就不会在中途看到库存从两边同时消失；加锁顺序固定下来，两个方向的转账也不会互相卡住对方等待的锁。
不锁目标仓库意味着别的线程能在 remove 和 add 之间看到货物凭空消失的窗口。
只检查不扣减根本没有真正转移库存，跟需求要求的原子转移完全不是一回事。
先加后查会让目标仓库先出现凭空多出来的库存，顺序反了会制造幻影数量。
optionExplanations_en: Holding the locks on each warehouse at the same time means no outside observer ever sees stock missing from both sides, and a fixed lock order stops two opposite-direction transfers from deadlocking each other.
Not locking the destination leaves a window where another thread can see the stock vanish between the remove and the add.
Only checking availability without actually deducting never moves any stock at all — that's not a transfer.
Adding to the destination before checking the source conjures phantom stock there first, the wrong order entirely.

scenario: 两个线程可能同时 EAST->WEST 和 WEST->EAST 转移。
scenario_en: Two threads may concurrently transfer EAST->WEST and WEST->EAST.
q: 这段实现为什么按 ID 排序后再加锁？
q_en: Why does this implementation sort IDs before locking?
options: 让字典序更好看
防止两个相反方向的 transfer 形成循环等待死锁
保证 EAST 永远是源仓库
让 removeStock 可以忽略库存不足
options_en: To make the lexical order look nicer.
To prevent two opposite-direction transfers from forming a circular-wait deadlock.
To guarantee EAST is always the source warehouse.
To let removeStock ignore insufficient stock.
why: 所有线程都按同一全局顺序获取锁，就不会出现 A 持有 EAST 等 WEST、B 持有 WEST 等 EAST 的循环等待。
why_en: Consistent lock ordering prevents deadlock when two threads transfer stock between the same pair of warehouses.
whenOtherWins: 如果只用数据库事务，锁顺序交给数据库和隔离级别处理，但应用层仍要理解死锁风险。
tradeoff: 全局锁顺序防死锁 vs 各自随意加锁更简单但会死锁
optionExplanations: 排序不是为了好看，而是给所有线程一个统一、可预测的加锁顺序。
只要每个线程抢锁的先后次序统一，就永远不会出现 A 攥着 EAST 干等 WEST、同时 B 攥着 WEST 干等 EAST 这种谁也让不了谁的死局。
排序结果取决于两个 ID 的字典序，谁是 source 谁是 target 由业务参数决定，跟这个无关。
锁的顺序只影响谁先拿到锁，不会改变 removeStock 内部对库存是否足够的判断逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting isn't about looking tidy — it gives every thread the same predictable lock order.

When every thread acquires locks in the same global order, you can never get A holding EAST while waiting on WEST and B holding WEST while waiting on EAST — that circular wait is exactly what deadlock needs.
Which ID sorts first depends on lexical order; which warehouse is actually the source comes from the call arguments, unrelated to this.
Lock order only decides who gets the lock first — it doesn't touch removeStock's own check for whether enough stock exists.

scenario: InventoryManager.transfer 在持有仓库锁期间，又调用了同样加锁的 Warehouse.removeStock/addStock。
scenario_en: InventoryManager.transfer holds warehouse locks and then calls Warehouse.removeStock/addStock, which also synchronize on the same Warehouse.
q: 为什么这个 atomic transfer 方案要求 reentrant locks？
q_en: Why does this atomic transfer design require reentrant locks?
options: reentrant locks 会在后台自动创建出新的库存
非重入锁天生执行速度更快，所以整个系统都必须使用它
已经持有 Warehouse 锁时再调用同锁的方法会再次获取同一把锁
只有 reentrant locks 这种锁才能用来比较字符串
options_en: Reentrant locks quietly create new inventory in the background on their own.
Non-reentrant locks are inherently faster, so the whole system has to use them.
While already holding the Warehouse lock, calling its own synchronized method acquires that same lock again.
Only reentrant locks, out of every lock type, can be used to compare strings.
why: 如果锁不可重入，线程持有仓库锁后调用内部同步方法会自我死锁；无重入语言需要暴露 non-locking 内部 helper。
why_en: Calling synchronized warehouse methods while already holding their locks requires reentrant locks or non-locking internal helpers.
tradeoff: 可重入锁简化嵌套调用 vs 不可重入锁需要额外的无锁 helper

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一线程可以对已持有的锁再次加锁而不会自我阻塞，如 Java 的 synchronized。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reentrant lock lets the same thread acquire a lock it already holds without blocking itself, like Java's synchronized.

optionExplanations: 锁的可重入性跟库存会不会被自动创建毫无关系，这个说法是无中生有。
这里选可重入锁不是为了追求速度，而是为了让嵌套加锁不至于自己把自己卡死。
transfer 已经拿着 Warehouse 锁，又调用同样加了锁的 removeStock/addStock，等于同一线程要对同一把锁再取一次，非重入锁会在这里自锁。
字符串比较是普通逻辑运算，跟锁是否可重入完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Whether a lock is reentrant has nothing to do with inventory getting created automatically — that's just made up.
Reentrant locking isn't chosen here for speed; it's chosen so nested locking doesn't lock the thread out of its own lock.
transfer already holds the Warehouse lock, then calls removeStock/addStock, which synchronize on that same lock — the same thread needs to acquire it again, which a non-reentrant lock would refuse.
String comparison is plain logic unrelated to whether a lock happens to be reentrant.

scenario: transfer 的 fromWarehouseId 和 toWarehouseId 相同。
scenario_en: A transfer call has the same fromWarehouseId and toWarehouseId.
q: 合理的处理方式是什么？
q_en: How should same-warehouse transfer be handled?
options: 执行 remove 再 add 同一仓库，并触发两次告警
直接删除这个仓库对象
随机挑一个目标仓库替代
返回 false 或视为 no-op，基础实现通常拒绝
options_en: Remove then add on the same warehouse and fire alerts twice.
Delete that warehouse object outright.
Pick a random destination warehouse instead.
Return false or treat it as a no-op; the base implementation usually rejects it.
why: 同仓库转移没有业务意义，且可能制造多余告警或锁问题；明确拒绝最简单。
why_en: A transfer from a warehouse to itself should be rejected or treated as a no-op by explicit design.
whenOtherWins: 如果 API 语义需要幂等 no-op，可以返回 true 且不改变任何状态。
tradeoff: 直接拒绝更简单 vs 幂等 no-op 对调用方更友好
optionExplanations: 同仓库转移执行 remove 再 add 净效果是零，还可能因为中间跌破阈值而多打一次不必要的告警。
转移请求跟删除仓库对象是两个完全不相关的操作，不该因为参数写错就销毁仓库。
调用方明确指定了目标，随机换一个完全违背了调用方的意图。
同仓库转移没有业务意义，直接拒绝或当成 no-op 处理最简单，也不会制造多余的告警或锁问题。
optionExplanations_en: Removing then adding on the same warehouse nets to zero anyway, and can fire an unnecessary alert if stock dips below threshold in between.
A transfer request and deleting the warehouse object are unrelated operations — a bad parameter shouldn't destroy the warehouse.
The caller explicitly named a destination; swapping in a random one ignores what they actually asked for.
A same-warehouse transfer has no business meaning, so rejecting it or treating it as a no-op is the simplest choice and avoids extra alerts or lock issues.

q: InventoryManager 的主要 API 包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which methods belong in the main InventoryManager API?
options: addStock(warehouseId,productId,quantity)
removeStock(warehouseId,productId,quantity)
transfer(productId,from,to,quantity)
getWarehousesWithAvailability(productId,quantity)
setLowStockAlert(warehouseId,productId,threshold,listener)
options_en: addStock(warehouseId, productId, quantity)
removeStock(warehouseId, productId, quantity)
transfer(productId, from, to, quantity)
getWarehousesWithAvailability(productId, quantity)
setLowStockAlert(warehouseId, productId, threshold, listener)
why: 这些方法对应最终需求，Manager 只负责查仓库和跨仓协调；实际库存状态仍由 Warehouse 拥有。
why_en: InventoryManager exposes add, remove, transfer, availability lookup, and alert configuration as its public API.
optionExplanations: addStock 是往指定仓库加库存的入口，属于最基础的写操作。
removeStock 对应扣减库存，需要额外处理库存不足的失败情况。
transfer 是唯一跨越两个仓库的写操作，需要更强的原子性保证。
getWarehousesWithAvailability 是履约前必须的只读查询。
setLowStockAlert 让调用方能配置阈值和通知渠道，这是告警功能对外暴露的入口。
optionExplanations_en: addStock is the entry point for adding to a specific warehouse, the most basic write.
removeStock covers deduction and has to handle the insufficient-stock failure case on top.
transfer is the one write that spans two warehouses at once, so it needs a stronger atomicity guarantee.
getWarehousesWithAvailability is the read-only lookup fulfillment needs before placing an order.
setLowStockAlert is how a caller configures a threshold and channel, the public entry point into the alert feature.

scenario: 调用 addStock 或 removeStock 时 quantity <= 0。
scenario_en: addStock or removeStock is called with quantity <= 0.
q: 应如何处理非法的 quantity？
q_en: How should invalid stock quantities be handled?
options: addStock 拒绝或抛错，removeStock 返回 false
把负数当成 removeStock，正数当 addStock 处理
把 0 当成信号，强制触发一次低库存告警
允许库存直接变负，之后再想办法修正差额
options_en: addStock rejects or throws, removeStock returns false; the quantity never changes.
Treat a negative addStock as a removeStock and a positive removeStock as an addStock.
Treat zero as a signal to force a low-stock alert.
Let the quantity go negative and fix the gap later.
why: 数量必须是正数才能表达库存变化；负数操作会绕过不变量并混淆 API 语义。
why_en: Stock mutation quantities should be positive, and invalid quantities should never change inventory.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要把库存直接调整到某个目标数，应设计单独的 setStock/adjustment API 并记录审计原因。
tradeoff: 早失败拒绝非法输入 vs 兼容负数换语义复杂
optionExplanations: quantity 必须是正整数才能对应一次真实变化，非法值直接拒绝、库存状态完全不动。
把符号当成操作类型的开关，会让调用方一旦传错符号就悄悄改变了自己本来的意图。
0 只是数量非法，跟阈值穿越是两回事，把它强行绑到告警上没有依据。
允许库存变负再想办法修正，跟库存不能为负这条不变量直接冲突。
optionExplanations_en: A quantity must be a positive integer to represent a real change, so invalid input is rejected outright and the state never moves.
Treating the sign as an operation switch means one wrong sign silently flips what the caller actually meant to do.
Zero is simply not a usable amount, unrelated to a threshold crossing — tying it to an alert has no basis.
Letting the count go negative and patching it up later directly conflicts with the never-negative invariant.

scenario: checkAvailability 和 removeStock 被不同线程同时调用同一个 Warehouse。
scenario_en: Different threads call checkAvailability and removeStock on the same Warehouse at the same time.
q: 为什么 checkAvailability 也要同步？
q_en: Why should checkAvailability be synchronized too?
options: 让查询变慢才算正确
保证读到一致的库存并具有正确的内存可见性
因为它会修改库存
因为 listener 要求同步
options_en: Slowing the query down is what makes it correct.
It guarantees a consistent read with correct memory visibility.
Because it mutates the inventory.
Because the listener requires synchronization.
why: 未同步的读可能看到陈旧或中间状态；对共享 map，读写都应遵守同一同步规则。
why_en: Synchronized reads ensure consistent and visible inventory state under concurrent access.
whenOtherWins: 读多写少的场景可以用读写锁优化，但仍要有明确的同步策略。
tradeoff: 全部同步保证一致性 vs 读写锁换更高读并发
optionExplanations: 查询变慢本身不能带来正确性，同步的目的是可见性，不是故意拖慢。
没同步的读可能拿到别的线程写到一半的中间状态；跟写方法遵守同一套同步规则，才能保证读到的是一致、最新的值。
checkAvailability 只读不写，它需要同步的原因跟修不修改库存无关。
listener 只在告警触发时才会被调用，跟这个方法是否要同步完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Being slower doesn't make a query correct; synchronization exists for visibility, not to intentionally slow things down.
A read taken outside any lock can catch another thread's half-finished write; following the same locking rule as writers guarantees a consistent, up-to-date value.
checkAvailability only reads, never mutates — the reason it needs synchronization has nothing to do with mutation.
The listener is only invoked when an alert fires, unrelated to whether checkAvailability itself needs to synchronize.

scenario: 调用 setLowStockAlert(productId, threshold, listener)，threshold=0 或 listener=null。
scenario_en: setLowStockAlert(productId, threshold, listener) is called with threshold=0 or listener=null.
q: 应该怎么处理无效的告警配置？
q_en: How should invalid alert configuration be handled?
options: 创建一个永远触发的告警
忽略 listener，只保存 threshold
拒绝这次配置
把 threshold 强制改成 1
options_en: Create an alert that always fires.
Ignore the listener and only save the threshold.
Reject the configuration.
Force the threshold to 1.
why: 低库存阈值必须为正，listener 不能为空，否则触发时无可执行的动作；配置错误应早失败。
why_en: Invalid alert thresholds or null listeners should be rejected when configuring alerts.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许 0 库存也报警，条件可以改成 threshold >= 0，但必须显式声明。
tradeoff: 早失败拒绝非法配置 vs 静默容错换来隐藏 bug
optionExplanations: 阈值或 listener 无效时造出一个永远触发的告警，只会制造无意义的噪音，不是合理的容错。
丢掉 listener 只留 threshold，等真正触发时根本没有对象可以通知，配置形同虚设。
阈值要求是正数、通知对象不能是空的，不然真触发那一刻根本没人可通知；这类错误应该在配置时就被挡下来。
把非法输入偷偷改成一个默认值，会掩盖调用方真正的错误，让 bug 更难被发现。
optionExplanations_en: Turning an invalid threshold or listener into an always-firing alert just produces noise, not sane error handling.
Dropping the listener and keeping only the threshold leaves nothing to actually notify once the alert would fire — the config becomes pointless.
The threshold must be positive and the listener non-null, or there's nothing to execute when it fires, so an invalid config gets turned away right here.
Silently coercing bad input into a default value hides the caller's real mistake and makes the bug harder to find.

q: 补全库存操作的返回语义：
q_en: Complete the return semantics for stock operations:
text: addStock 通常返回 {{void}}，因为加库存总可成功；removeStock 返回 {{boolean}}，因为库存不足时可能失败。
why: API 返回值应反映操作是否有可预期失败；加库存失败一般是无效仓库或参数错误，用异常更清晰。
why_en: addStock can be void while removeStock returns success because only removal can fail from insufficient stock.

scenario: 电商结账需要 5 分钟，不能让两个用户都看到“最后 1 件可买”并在付款时才失败。
scenario_en: Checkout can take 5 minutes, and two users should not both see the last unit as buyable and only fail after payment.
q: 应加入哪种机制解决这个问题？
q_en: What mechanism should be added to prevent this oversell window?
options: 只在用户支付成功之后，才真正去检查库存是否够
先把库存直接扣成负数，事后再异步补偿差额
直接把这件商品永久锁死，谁都不能再下单购买它
加入 reservation 机制：先预占再确认或释放
options_en: Only actually check whether inventory is enough after the user's payment already succeeds.
Deduct the stock straight into negative first, then compensate the gap asynchronously later.
Lock this product down permanently so that nobody can ever place an order for it again.
Add a reservation mechanism: hold stock first, then confirm or release it.
why: reservation 把 physical stock 与 reserved stock 分开，结账开始时占用可售数量，付款成功再真正扣减。
why_en: A reservation system holds available inventory during checkout and confirms or releases it later.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务采用乐观售卖并接受缺货退款，可以不做 reservation，在订单确认后再补救。
tradeoff: reservation 保证结账不落空 vs 乐观售卖更简单但可能超卖
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["checkout starts"] --> B{"available = inventory - reserved"}
B -->|enough| C["create Reservation"]
C --> D["increase reserved"]
D --> E{"payment result"}
E -->|success| F["confirm: reduce inventory and reserved"]
E -->|timeout/cancel| G["release: reduce reserved"]
optionExplanations: 结账开始时不预占，两个用户都能看到还有货，等到都付款成功才发现只有一件，超卖已经发生了。
先让库存变负再补偿，意味着系统在补偿完成前一直处于错误状态，跟场景要求的正确性不符。
把商品永久锁死连正常售卖都做不了，跟结账期间临时占用完全不是同一个诉求。
结账开始就先占用这部分可售数量，付款成功才真正扣减，超时或取消则释放，两个用户不会同时看到同一件货能买。
optionExplanations_en: Not holding anything at checkout start lets two users both see the last unit as available, and overselling only surfaces after both payments succeed.
Letting stock go negative and compensating afterward means the system stays wrong the whole time until that compensation lands, which is not what this scenario needs.
Locking the product permanently blocks normal selling entirely, a very different ask from just holding it during one checkout.

Holding the available quantity the moment checkout starts, deducting for real only on payment success, and releasing on timeout or cancel keeps two users from ever seeing the same unit as buyable at once.

q: 引入库存 reservation 后 Warehouse 需要新增哪些状态？（多选）
q_en: Which new state does Warehouse need after adding reservations?
options: reserved: Map<productId,int>
reservations: Map<reservationId,Reservation>
Reservation(productId,quantity,expiresAt)
每个产品的图片 URL
options_en: reserved: Map<productId,int>
reservations: Map<reservationId,Reservation>
A Reservation(productId, quantity, expiresAt) record.
An image URL for every product.
why: available = inventory - reserved；reservation 记录过期时间，支持后续确认或释放。
why_en: Inventory reservations require reserved counts, reservation records, and expiration timestamps.
optionExplanations: reserved 记录每个产品已经被占用但还没真正扣减的数量，可售库存要靠库存总量减去这部分占用才算得出来。
reservations 让每一次预占都能被单独追踪、确认或释放，而不是只有一个笼统的计数。
这条记录本身需要产品、数量和到期时间，才能知道这份占用什么时候该被清理。
图片 URL 属于产品目录信息，本系统只按 productId 计数，不该把这类展示数据塞进来。
optionExplanations_en: reserved tracks how much of each product is held but not yet actually deducted — available stock only comes from subtracting it out of inventory.
reservations lets each individual hold be tracked, confirmed, or released on its own instead of collapsing into one blunt counter.
This kind of record needs to capture the product, quantity, and an expiry time so the system knows when that hold should be cleaned up.
An image URL belongs to the product catalog; this service only tracks productId counts and shouldn't absorb display data like that.

q: 库存 reservation 的正确流程是什么？
q_en: What is the correct reservation flow for inventory?
steps: reserveStock 检查 inventory - reserved 是否足够。
创建 Reservation(productId, quantity, expiresAt)。
增加 reserved[productId]。
支付成功时 confirmReservation 扣减 inventory、减少 reserved、删除 reservation。
超时或放弃时 releaseReservation 减少 reserved、删除 reservation。
why: reservation 不立即减少 physical inventory，但会减少可售库存；确认和释放是两条互斥的后续路径。
why_en: Reservation reserves available quantity first, then either confirms into real removal or releases the hold.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> RESERVED : reserveStock
RESERVED --> CONFIRMED : payment success
RESERVED --> RELEASED : cancel or timeout
CONFIRMED --> [*]
RELEASED --> [*]

scenario: 用户关掉浏览器，没有主动调用 releaseReservation。
scenario_en: The user closes the browser and never calls releaseReservation.
q: 系统还需要补什么机制？
q_en: What mechanism is still needed for abandoned reservations?
options: 后台任务周期扫描并释放已过期的 reservation
永远保留 reserved 数量
等下一次 addStock 自动删除所有 reservation
让 AlertListener 负责清库存
options_en: A background job periodically scans and releases expired reservations.
Keep the reserved quantity locked forever.
Let the next addStock silently delete all reservations.
Let AlertListener clear the inventory.
why: 没有清理，reserved 库存会永久锁住；超时值是业务权衡，常见 5-15 分钟。
why_en: Expired reservation cleanup is needed so abandoned checkouts do not hold inventory forever.
whenOtherWins: 如果用外部 TTL 存储，过期可由存储层驱动，但仍要处理释放 reserved 的一致性。
tradeoff: 定期清理换来可售库存及时释放 vs 不清理实现更简单但库存被锁死
optionExplanations: 没有人主动释放时，只能靠后台任务定期扫描已到期的 reservation 并释放，可售库存才不会被无限期占住。
永远不释放意味着一次没完成的结账会永久锁死这部分库存，可售数量只会越攒越少。
addStock 加的是完全不相关产品或仓库的库存，把它跟清理别的 reservation 绑在一起没有道理。
AlertListener 只负责通知低库存，清理到期预占完全不是它的职责。
optionExplanations_en: With no one calling release, only a background job that periodically scans and clears out stale holds keeps the sellable count from being locked away forever.
Never releasing means one checkout that was simply walked away from permanently locks that stock up, and the sellable count only ever shrinks.
addStock adds to a completely unrelated product or warehouse — tying it to cleaning up someone else's reservation makes no sense.
AlertListener only handles low-stock notifications; cleaning up lapsed holds was never its job.

scenario: 仓库转移真实需要 3-5 天运输，库存不该在源和目标间瞬间移动。
scenario_en: A real warehouse transfer takes 3-5 days, so stock should not instantly jump from source to destination.
q: 更真实的建模方式是什么？
q_en: What is the more realistic model for warehouse transfers?
options: 仍然同时 remove source 和 add destination
把 Transfer 建成能持有库存的一等实体
把库存从系统总量中直接删除
把目标仓库提前加上库存
options_en: Still remove from source and add to destination at the same instant.
Model Transfer as a first-class entity that can hold in-transit inventory.
Delete the stock from the system total entirely.
Add the stock to the destination early, before it arrives.
why: 运输中库存不在任一仓库可售，但仍属于系统总量；Transfer 作为临时 holder 能准确表达在途状态。
why_en: A first-class Transfer entity can hold in-transit inventory without making it available at either warehouse.
whenOtherWins: 面试基础范围内可以用原子瞬移 transfer，简单满足需求即可。
tradeoff: 建模在途状态更真实 vs 原子瞬移实现更简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
S["source warehouse"] -->|ship| X["Transfer holder"]
X -->|arrive| T["target warehouse"]
X --> Q["in transit stock"]
Q --> N["not sellable but counted in system total"]
optionExplanations: 瞬间搬移完全忽略了真实运输要花 3-5 天这个约束，跟场景要求的真实建模不符。
运输途中的库存哪个仓库都卖不了，但仍属于系统总量，把 Transfer 建成能临时持有库存的实体正好表达这个状态。
运输中的货依然存在，只是暂时不在任何仓库里，直接从系统总量里删掉会让库存凭空消失。
货还没到就先加到目标仓库，会让还在路上的库存被提前当成可售库存卖出去。
optionExplanations_en: Instant teleportation ignores the given constraint that real transport takes 3-5 days, contradicting the realistic modeling this scenario asks for.
Stock on the road can't be bought from either location right now, but it's still part of the system total — modeling Transfer as an entity that can temporarily hold it captures exactly that state.
Stock in transit still exists, just not inside any warehouse yet; deleting it from the system total would make it vanish into thin air.
Adding it to the destination before it arrives lets stock that's still on the road get sold as if it were already there.

scenario: 把 Transfer 建成一个可以临时持有库存的实体，而不是让库存在两仓库间瞬移。
scenario_en: Transfer is modeled as an entity that can temporarily hold inventory instead of teleporting stock between warehouses.
q: Transfer as InventoryHolder 的“aha”是什么？
q_en: What is the key idea behind Transfer as an InventoryHolder?
options: Transfer 必须继承 Warehouse 所有行为
在途库存应该可以直接被售卖
库存可以暂时存在于仓库以外的持有者中，系统总量仍可核对
完成 transfer 不需要目标仓库
options_en: Transfer must inherit every behavior of Warehouse.
In-transit stock should be directly sellable.
Stock can temporarily live in a holder outside any warehouse while the system total still reconciles.
Completing a transfer needs no destination warehouse.
why: 把 Transfer 看作临时库存容器，能同时支持查询总库存和禁止在途库存履约。
why_en: Modeling Transfer as an inventory holder accounts for in-transit stock without making it available for orders.
tradeoff: 临时持有者建模更真实 vs 只用 Warehouse 更简单

termDefinitions.meaning: 任何能持有库存数量的实体的抽象，Warehouse 和 Transfer 都可以是一种 holder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InventoryHolder is an abstraction for anything that can hold a stock quantity; both Warehouse and Transfer can be one.

optionExplanations: Transfer 只需要能持有一小段库存量，不需要继承 Warehouse 的告警、锁这些完整行为。
在途库存正是不能直接售卖的那部分，这也是为什么要单独建模，让它既计入总量又不可履约。
把库存的容身之处从只能是仓库扩展成任何 holder，运输途中的量就能被系统总量核对到，同时又不会被当成可售库存。
transfer 完成时依然要把货物加进目标仓库，目标仓库这一步没法省略。
optionExplanations_en: Transfer only needs to hold a small quantity temporarily, not inherit Warehouse's full behavior like alerting and locking.
Stock that's still on the road is precisely the part that must not be sellable — that's the whole reason it gets modeled separately.
Widening where stock can live from just warehouses to any holder lets in-transit quantity still reconcile against the system total while staying unavailable to sell.
Completing a transfer still has to add the stock into the destination warehouse — that step can't be skipped.

q: 在途 Transfer 实体通常保存哪些信息？（多选）
q_en: What information does an in-transit Transfer usually store?
options: id
productId 和 quantity
fromWarehouseId 和 toWarehouseId
createdAt 或状态
options_en: id
productId and quantity
fromWarehouseId and toWarehouseId
createdAt or a status field
why: 这些字段让系统知道哪批库存、从哪来、到哪去、是否完成；完成时再把库存加入目标仓库。
why_en: A transfer record identifies the in-transit product, quantity, endpoints, and its own status over time.
optionExplanations: id 让每一次转移能被单独追踪和引用。
productId 和 quantity 记录这批在途货物具体是什么、有多少。
fromWarehouseId 和 toWarehouseId 说明这批货从哪来、要去哪。
createdAt 或状态字段让系统知道这次转移进行到哪一步、该不该完成。
optionExplanations_en: id lets each individual transfer be tracked and referenced on its own.
productId and quantity record exactly what's in transit and how much of it.
fromWarehouseId and toWarehouseId say where this batch came from and where it's headed.
createdAt or a status field tells the system what stage this transfer is at and whether it should complete.

scenario: 有人想在基础设计里再加入订单处理、支付、仓库服务范围和产品目录。
scenario_en: Someone asks to add order processing, payment, serviceability, and product catalog features to the base design.
q: 面对这个扩展请求应该怎么处理？
q_en: How should this scope-expansion request be handled?
options: 全部塞进 InventoryManager
让 Warehouse 负责支付
把 productId 替换成 Product 复杂对象
明确这些属于 out of scope，保持库存核心模型
options_en: Cram everything into InventoryManager.
Let Warehouse handle payment.
Replace productId with a full Product object.
State these are out of scope and keep the core inventory model focused.
why: 库存系统只管理数量和库存相关操作；订单、支付、产品目录是独立系统，会显著扩大设计。
why_en: Order processing, payment, serviceability, and catalog management are outside the scoped inventory model.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求扩展到订单系统，再增加 Order/Reservation/Fulfillment 等实体。
tradeoff: 守住范围保持模型简单 vs 扩大范围覆盖更多需求
optionExplanations: 把订单、支付、产品目录全塞进 InventoryManager，会让它同时承担好几个不相关系统的职责。
支付涉及的资金和第三方网关，跟 Warehouse 管理库存数量完全是两个领域。
把 productId 换成完整 Product 对象，等于把产品目录这个外部系统的职责搬进了库存系统。
订单、支付、产品目录都是独立系统，明确它们不在范围内，库存核心模型才能保持聚焦、不失控地膨胀。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming checkout, billing, and the product catalog into InventoryManager makes it own several unrelated systems' responsibilities at once.
Payment involves money and third-party gateways, an entirely different domain from Warehouse managing stock counts.
Swapping productId for a full Product object drags the catalog system's responsibilities into the inventory system.
Checkout, billing, and the catalog are separate systems in their own right; declaring them out of scope keeps the core stock-tracking design focused instead of letting it balloon without limits.

q: 原子转移 EAST -> WEST 5 件的正确状态变化是什么？
q_en: What are the correct state changes for an atomic EAST-to-WEST transfer of 5 units?
steps: 按稳定顺序锁住 EAST 和 WEST。
在锁内调用 EAST.removeStock，确认库存足够并扣到 2。
在仍持有两把锁时调用 WEST.addStock，加到 5。
释放两把锁并返回 true。
why: 锁持有期间外部线程不能看到缺失中间态；remove 失败则不 add，两个仓库保持原状。
why_en: Atomic transfer locks both warehouses, removes from source, adds to destination, and releases locks only after completion.

scenario: 低库存告警触发时，listener 需要知道具体是哪一个仓库缺货。
scenario_en: When a low-stock alert fires, the listener needs to know which warehouse is short on stock.
q: Warehouse 为什么需要自己的 id 字段？
q_en: Why does Warehouse need its own id field?
options: 把 warehouseId 传给 onLowStock 这个回调
用来决定这个产品当前对外销售的具体挂牌价格
用来在系统内部悄悄替代掉原本的 productId 这整个字段
用来生成专门保护这整个仓库状态的锁对象
options_en: To pass warehouseId to the onLowStock callback.
To decide the specific listed price this product is currently being sold at.
To quietly swap out the entire productId field internally without anyone noticing.
To generate the lock object that specifically guards this whole warehouse's state.
why: 告警没有 warehouseId 就无法判断哪处库存不足；Warehouse 自己持有 id 是最短路径。
why_en: Warehouse stores its own ID so low-stock notifications can identify which location is reporting.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有回调都统一经过 Manager 转发并由它补上下文，Warehouse 也能不存 id，但那样 Warehouse 要反过来依赖 Manager 传参。
tradeoff: 自持 id 传给回调 vs 让 Manager 补充上下文更绕

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识一个实体（这里是仓库）的字符串或数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ID, short for identifier, is the string or number that uniquely names one entity, here a warehouse.

optionExplanations: 告警触发时 listener 需要知道是哪个仓库缺货，仓库把自己的标识随身带着，才能把它塞进 onLowStock 这个回调参数里。
定价属于产品目录或订单系统的职责，跟仓库的身份标识毫无关系。
id 标识的是仓库，productId 标识的是产品，两者是完全不同维度的字段，不能互相替代。
锁对象是 Warehouse 内部用来做并发控制的机制，跟对外暴露的仓库 id 是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: The listener needs to know which warehouse is short when an alert fires, and Warehouse holding its own id is what lets it pass that into the onLowStock callback.
Pricing belongs to the catalog or order system, unrelated to a warehouse's own identity.
id identifies the warehouse and productId identifies the product — two different dimensions that can't substitute for each other.
A lock object is Warehouse's internal concurrency-control mechanism, a separate thing from the id it exposes externally.

scenario: 低库存 alert 配置需要放在 Warehouse 还是 InventoryManager 里。
scenario_en: The low-stock alert configuration could live in Warehouse or InventoryManager.
q: 为什么低库存 alert 配置应放在 Warehouse？
q_en: Why should low-stock alert configuration live in Warehouse?
options: Manager 从架构设计上就完全不能访问任何一个仓库
告警是某仓库某产品的库存状态规则，Warehouse 拥有相关数量变化
AlertConfig 需要知道所有仓库库存加起来的总量
listener 只能在 Manager 内部的代码里被调用
options_en: By design, Manager is architecturally unable to reach into any warehouse at all.
An alert is a per-warehouse per-product rule, and Warehouse owns the quantity changes that trigger it.
AlertConfig would need to know the summed quantity across every single warehouse.
A listener can only ever be invoked from code that lives inside Manager.
why: Warehouse 最懂自己产品数量的变化，能在 add/remove 后直接判断阈值穿越；Manager 只负责路由和跨仓协调。
why_en: Alert configuration belongs to Warehouse because it owns the per-product quantity changes that trigger alerts.
tradeoff: 配置贴近状态所有者 vs 集中放在 Manager 更容易全局管理
optionExplanations: InventoryManager 持有全部 Warehouse 的引用，访问仓库从来不是问题。
告警本质是这个仓库这个产品的库存状态规则，而数量变化正好发生在 Warehouse 内部，配置贴着变化发生的地方最直接。
阈值判断只看这一个仓库这一个产品的数量穿越，不需要知道其他仓库的库存。
listener 是在 add/remove 之后被 Warehouse 自己收集触发的，调用点不在 Manager。
optionExplanations_en: InventoryManager holds a reference to every Warehouse, so access was never the obstacle.
An alert is really a rule about one warehouse's one product, and the number that moves to trigger it changes inside Warehouse — placing the config right where that happens is the most direct path.
The threshold check only looks at this one warehouse's quantity crossing, with no need to know any other warehouse's stock.
The listener gets collected and fired by Warehouse itself right after add/remove, not from inside Manager.

scenario: 需求明确仓库是固定集合，在系统初始化时一次性创建。
scenario_en: The requirements say warehouses are a fixed set created once during initialization.
q: InventoryManager 构造函数应如何处理 warehouseIds？
q_en: How should the InventoryManager constructor handle warehouseIds?
options: 每次 addStock 时懒创建任意 warehouseId
忽略传入的 ids
遍历 ids，创建 Warehouse(id) 并放入 map
要求调用方自己传 Warehouse map 且不做校验
options_en: Lazily create any warehouseId the first time addStock sees it.
Ignore the ids that are passed in.
Iterate the ids, create a Warehouse(id) for each, and store them in the map.
Require the caller to pass a pre-built Warehouse map with no validation.
why: 固定启动配置让 Manager 在构造时建立完整仓库集合；无效 warehouseId 后续应快速失败。
why_en: The manager eagerly creates every configured warehouse at startup because the warehouse set is fixed.
whenOtherWins: 如果仓库集合会动态增删，就需要额外的 addWarehouse/removeWarehouse 接口，而不是只在构造时建一次。
tradeoff: 启动时一次性创建 vs 运行时懒创建换灵活性
optionExplanations: 需求已经说明仓库集合是固定的，运行时才懒创建等于放弃了这条前提，还会让无效 id 悄悄通过。
构造函数收到的 ids 就是仓库集合的来源，直接忽略等于系统启动后没有任何仓库可用。
仓库集合固定不变，在构造时一次性遍历 ids 建好完整的 Warehouse map，这样任何不存在的 id 后面调用时就能立刻报错。
不做校验意味着任何格式错误或重复的 id 都能直接进入系统，把本该在构造期发现的问题推给了运行期。
optionExplanations_en: The requirements already say which warehouses exist is decided once and never changes; lazily creating at runtime abandons that premise and lets invalid ids slip through quietly.
The ids passed into the constructor are the only source telling the system which warehouses to create — ignoring them leaves nothing built at startup.
Since the roster never changes after startup, iterating the ids once at construction to build the full Warehouse map lets any later invalid warehouseId fail fast immediately.
Skipping validation lets any malformed or duplicate id straight into the system, pushing a problem that belongs at construction time into runtime instead.

scenario: removeStock 把库存从 15 扣到 9，阈值是 10。
scenario_en: removeStock changes stock from 15 to 9, and the alert threshold is 10.
q: getAlertsToFire 这次应返回什么？
q_en: What should getAlertsToFire return for this update?
options: null，因为库存仍非零
立即调用 listener 并持锁等待
删除这个产品的 alert config
包含该阈值 listener 的 alert 列表
options_en: null, because the stock is still non-zero.
Call the listener immediately while still holding the lock.
Delete the alert config for this product.
A list of alerts containing the listener for that threshold.
why: 阈值从上方穿越到下方，应收集待触发的告警；真正的回调在释放锁后才执行。
why_en: Downward threshold crossing should collect the matching listeners so they can fire after the lock is released.
whenOtherWins: 如果 newQty 恰好等于 threshold，按 < threshold 的规则不触发；若业务定义为 <=，条件要相应调整。
tradeoff: 锁内只收集列表 vs 锁内直接触发换来更简单但危险的实现
optionExplanations: 库存非零不代表没有跌破阈值，9 依然低于 10 这个阈值，这里明显发生了一次下穿。
在锁内直接调用 listener 会让慢 I/O 占住仓库锁，这正是这个方法要避免的问题。
阈值穿越只是应该触发一次通知，不代表这条告警规则以后都不需要了，删除配置没有依据。
prevQty=15 高于阈值、newQty=9 低于阈值，正好是一次下穿，应该把对应的 listener 收集进列表，等释放锁后再触发。
optionExplanations_en: Nonzero stock doesn't mean nothing crossed — 9 is still below the threshold of 10, so a downward crossing clearly happened.
Calling the listener directly inside the lock is exactly the slow-I/O-holds-the-lock problem this method is designed to avoid.
Dipping below the threshold just means one notification should fire, not that the rule is done forever — deleting the config has no basis.
prevQty=15 is above threshold and newQty=9 is below it, exactly a downward crossing, so its listener belongs in the return list and only actually fires once the lock releases.

q: Senior 级库存题回答应主动覆盖哪些点？（多选）
q_en: Which points should a senior-level inventory-system answer proactively cover?
options: transfer 的 TOCTOU race
同时锁两个仓库并按稳定顺序防死锁
reentrant lock 或 non-locking helper 的要求
告警回调放锁外触发
reservation/in-transit 等扩展
options_en: The TOCTOU race inside a naive transfer.
Locking both warehouses at once in a stable order to prevent deadlock.
The reentrant-lock requirement, or a non-locking internal helper as its alternative.
Firing alert callbacks outside the lock.
Extensions such as reservation or in-transit modeling.
why: 高级回答的重点是并发正确性和业务状态演进；单纯的 Map 加减不足以覆盖题目的风险点。
why_en: Senior inventory answers focus on transfer races, ordered locking, reentrancy, alert callbacks outside locks, and realistic extensions.
optionExplanations: TOCTOU race 是 naive transfer 最容易被面试官追问出来的漏洞，主动提到说明想清楚了并发问题。
同时锁两个仓库并按固定顺序，是把看起来原子变成真正原子且不死锁的关键。
reentrant lock 或者拆出无锁 helper，是嵌套调用同步方法时躲不开的一个细节。
把慢 I/O 的回调放到锁外触发，避免了吞吐和死锁两个问题同时暴露。
reservation、in-transit 这些扩展说明候选人能从基础功能正确走到更贴近真实业务这一步。
optionExplanations_en: The TOCTOU race is the bug interviewers most often probe for in a naive transfer, so raising it first shows real concurrency thinking.
Locking both warehouses at once in a fixed order is what turns 'looks atomic' into actually atomic and deadlock-free.
Reentrant locks, or a non-locking internal helper as the alternative, is a detail nested synchronized calls can't dodge.
Keeping slow-I/O notifications out of the locked section avoids exposing both a throughput problem and a deadlock risk at once.
Extensions like reservation and in-transit modeling show moving from basic functionality working toward something closer to real business needs.

q: 按顺序排列库存系统主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main inventory-system design chain in order:
steps: Product 降级为 productId key，Warehouse 成为库存状态拥有者。
澄清多仓库库存、add/remove、availability、transfer、alerts、thread-safe。
InventoryManager 作为 facade 路由单仓操作并协调跨仓操作。
AlertConfig/AlertListener 解耦阈值和通知渠道。
Warehouse 方法用锁保护库存，transfer 额外按顺序锁两仓库。
why: 这条链路从范围和实体裁剪，到职责分层、通知解耦和并发正确性。
why_en: The design chain moves from scope to entity pruning, orchestration, alert abstraction, and concurrency correctness.

scenario: 面试最后让你总结库存系统最重要的不变量。
scenario_en: At the end of the interview, you are asked to summarize the most important inventory-system invariants.
q: 哪一个总结最准确？
q_en: Which summary best captures the core invariant?
options: 任何仓库任何产品库存都不能为负，transfer 要保持系统总量不变
低库存这件事必须在每一次查询发生时都重新报警一次
所有仓库无论什么时候都必须持有完全一模一样数量的库存
transfer 执行过程中应当被允许让库存短暂地凭空丢失掉一部分
options_en: No warehouse's product quantity may go negative, and a transfer must keep the system total unchanged.
Low stock has to trigger a brand-new alert on literally every single query that runs.
Every warehouse, at every moment, must hold exactly the identical quantity of stock.
A transfer should be allowed to let some stock briefly vanish into thin air while it runs.
why: 非负库存和原子 transfer 是库存系统正确性的核心；告警只是附加通知，不应破坏库存不变量。
why_en: The core invariant is non-negative per-warehouse stock and atomic cross-warehouse transfers when strict consistency is required.
whenOtherWins: 如果建模了在途库存，transfer 不再是瞬移，但系统总库存仍应在 Warehouse 和 Transfer holder 间守恒。
tradeoff: 严格原子 transfer 保证不变量 vs 允许在途状态换取更真实的建模
optionExplanations: 非负库存和转移前后系统总量不变，这两条是贯穿整个设计、任何操作都不能违反的底线。
重复报警只会制造噪音，告警机制专门设计成只在下穿阈值那一刻触发一次，这条总结正好说反了。
不同仓库本来就该按各自的销量和补货独立变化，要求库存处处相同没有任何业务依据。
凭空丢失库存正是 transfer 要用双锁原子性极力避免的问题，允许它发生等于放弃了这条不变量。
optionExplanations_en: Never letting any warehouse's count go negative, and keeping the system total unchanged across a transfer, are the floor that no operation is allowed to cross.
Repeated alerts just create noise — the whole point of the crossing-based design is to fire once, so this summary has it backwards.
Different warehouses are expected to move independently with their own sales and restocking; requiring identical stock everywhere has no business basis.
Losing stock into thin air is exactly what the two-lock atomic transfer exists to prevent — allowing it means abandoning that invariant.
